_comment: THE SHARED CONTRACT between agent-team-template's validateArming (scripts/lib/arm.mjs) and
agent-cockpit's armingProblems (api/state.js). The two are mirrored by hand, not imported -
there is no import path between a student's repo and a deployed web app - so drift is the
standing risk, and it has happened twice.
This file is the same bytes in both repos. Each repo has a test that runs ITS implementation
over these cases and asserts the exact problem list. Change the logic on one side only and
that side's test fails on the next run.
KEEP IN SYNC: tests/fixtures/arming-parity.json in agent-team-template and agent-cockpit.
name: Monday Brief

cases.label: armed with a schedule - the ordinary working job
off, with no reason - the silence has to be a decision somebody made
expected: Monday Brief: is not armed and carries no reason - say what would have to change for it to be worth a run

cases.label: a reason of nothing but spaces is no reason
expected: Monday Brief: is not armed and carries no reason - say what would have to change for it to be worth a run

cases.label: no trigger.armed field at all - never armed by default, and still owes a reason
expected: Monday Brief: is not armed and carries no reason - say what would have to change for it to be worth a run

cases.label: armed: "yes" - the wrong kind of true, which used to read as OFF in silence
expected: Monday Brief: trigger.armed must be true or false

cases.label: armed: "yes" with nothing else - the type problem does not swallow the reason problem
expected: Monday Brief: trigger.armed must be true or false
Monday Brief: is not armed and carries no reason - say what would have to change for it to be worth a run

cases.label: armed with no clock of any kind - a routine nobody could have created
expected: Monday Brief: is armed but declares no schedule - there is nothing for a routine to fire on

cases.label: a schedule of nothing but spaces is no schedule
expected: Monday Brief: is armed but declares no schedule - there is nothing for a routine to fire on

CLOCKLESS: an armed dashboard button is the same object a webhook posts to
CLOCKLESS: an unarmed webhook is not off - it has nothing to be off from
CLOCKLESS: an unarmed button job is not asked to justify a state it was never in
the exemption must NOT leak: a button job that also carries a schedule still owes a reason
expected: Monday Brief: is not armed and carries no reason - say what would have to change for it to be worth a run

cases.label: the exemption must NOT leak: a scheduled webhook job still owes a reason when off
expected: Monday Brief: is not armed and carries no reason - say what would have to change for it to be worth a run
